title: Queue-hop span enricher and Tempo forwarder for async workers
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Add a lightweight enrichment layer in the tracing pipeline that inserts synthetic 'queue-hop' spans and preserves original trace identifiers when traces traverse asynchronous worker queues (e.g. Kafka/SQS). The adapter will forward enriched OTLP spans to Tempo while preserving sampling and avoiding duplicate span collisions from retries.

Why: We frequently lose visibility into cross-service latency when work is decoupled through queues. Current traces break at producer/consumer boundaries and it is hard to attribute queue wait time vs processing time in dashboards and SLO debugging. This ticket implements an egress adapter that: (1) attaches queue metadata as attributes, (2) synthesizes queue-hop spans to make queue wait visible in flamegraphs, (3) deduplicates retry-induced duplicate spans, and (4) forwards efficiently to Tempo with tenant affinity.

Success criteria (measurable):
- Queue wait time appears as a first-class span for 95% of consumer traces from instrumented queues.
- No more than 1% increase in tracing pipeline p95 latency at 99th percentile for normal traffic after rollout.
- Duplicate span rate due to retries reduced by >= 90% for instrumented flows.
- Grafana dashboard added and used by at least two teams within 2 weeks of rollout.

Design notes / approach:
- Ingress: OTLP receiver (existing) passes spans to the enrichment module in the trace broker.
- Enrichment rules: if span contains queue metadata (message.id, queue.name, published_timestamp), create a synthetic span with: name: queue.hop, attributes: queue.name, queue.partition, message.id, produced_ts, consumer_received_ts. Synthetic span connects producer span -> synthetic queue.hop -> consumer span using original traceId and deterministic spanId derived from message.id (hash-based) to avoid collisions while keeping dedup semantics.
- Deduplication: maintain a short-lived LRU cache keyed by (tenant, message.id) storing recently observed synthetic spanIds and a TTL of 5m. On duplicate incoming consumer deliveries within TTL, skip emitting a second synthetic span. Cache backed by local in-memory sharded store with optional Redis fallback for cross-instance dedupe in dedicated clusters.
- Backpressure & resilience: enrichment is best-effort. If the local dedupe cache is overloaded or the enrichment module is >500ms processing latency, the pipeline falls back to pass-through (no synthetic spans) and emits a metric 'tracing.enrichment.fallback' and triggers SLO alert. We will implement a circuit-breaker that opens when enrichment error rate or latency exceeds thresholds.
- Tempo forwarding: keep batch sizes aligned with existing tempo exporter (max batch 200 spans or 100ms flush) and include tenant header routing so requests hit tenant-affine Tempo ingesters.

Trade-offs & alternatives considered:
- Option A: Inject synthetic spans at producer/consumer SDK level. Pros: precise local context. Cons: needs SDK changes across many services and rollout complexity.
- Option B (chosen): Central enrichment in trace broker. Pros: single place to improve visibility without code changes. Cons: inferred context may be less precise; requires dedupe and careful rate control to avoid pipeline amplification.

Implementation plan (high-level tasks):
1) Prototype enrichment module in trace broker (ENG-128412).
2) Add deterministic spanId generation util and sharded LRU cache with Redis fallback (ENG-128413).
3) Integrate enrichment into OTLP processing path behind feature flag per-tenant.
4) End-to-end test harness that replays annotated Kafka traces and asserts synthetic spans and dedupe.
5) Deploy canary to low-risk tenants for 2 weeks, monitor metrics/dashboards.
6) Gradual rollout with per-tenant opt-in and automatic rollback conditions.

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests for spanId derivation, TTL cache, and attribute mapping.
- Load test: synthetic Kafka replay at 2x production QPS for 30 minutes to measure p50/p95/p99 latency and enrichment CPU/memory.
- Integration test: assert correctness of Tempo traces in local devstack and staging Tempo instance.

Observability & dashboards:
- New Grafana dashboard: 'Queue-hop tracing - enrichment health' showing enrichment success rate, enrichment latency histogram, dedupe cache hit ratio, and downstream Tempo ingress metrics.
- Tracing SLO: track percent of consumer spans containing linked queue.hop span.

Rollout & mitigation:
- Feature-flagged per-tenant rollouts, default off.
- Monitor 'tracing.enrichment.fallback' and 'tracing.enrichment.error' metrics; auto-disable enrichment for tenant on >0.1% error rate sustained for 5 minutes.
- Quick rollback via feature flag and config toggle in Console.

Security & privacy:
- Queue attributes must be vetted; message payloads must not be included. We will ensure only allowed metadata keys are copied. Security review required per release.

2026-03-04: implemented deterministic spanId util and added unit tests; PR opened https://github.com/redwood-inference/trace-broker/pull/4512. Feedback: need TTL tuning and eviction metrics. Action: add cache metrics and Redis fallback plan.
2026-03-06: bench experiment shows enrichment adds ~7ms median and ~45ms p99 in broker path at low QPS; added circuit-breaker plan to reduce amplified overhead under load.
2026-03-09: Security review kickoff with Mira Koh; confirmed disallowed copying of message payloads and approved list of allowed queue attributes (queue.name, partition, message.id, produced_ts).
2026-03-10: Feature-flag gating implemented; canary rollout plan drafted. Next: run replay load test and publish dashboard to staging.
